title: FERC Compliance Directives — Docket P-10661-000: Letter to American Electric Power discussing the 06/02/2026 Dam Safety Inspection of the Constantine Hydroelectric Project under P-10661.
text:
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION
Office of Energy Projects
Division of Dam Safety and Inspections
Chicago Regional Office
In reply refer to: P-10661
July 2, 2026
VIA ELECTRONIC MAIL
Mr. Gene F. Sirca, Jr., Ph.D., P.E., S.E.
Chief Hydro Dam Safety Engineer
American Electric Power
gfsirca@aep.com
Re: Constantine Hydroelectric Project, FERC No. 10661
- 2026 Dam Safety Inspection (DSI) Follow-up
- 2025 Dam Safety Surveillance and Monitoring Report (DSSMR)
Dear Mr. Sirca:
The 2026 Dam Safety Inspection of Constantine Hydroelectric Project,
FERC No. 10661 was conducted on June 2, 2026, by Mr. Eduardo Prieto, P.E. of the
FERC Chicago Regional Office. He was accompanied by Mses. Justine Penix and
Jodi Slough, and Messrs. Rich Walag, Erwin Supranata, Rob Beller, Craig Bonesteel and
yourself of American Electric Power (AEP). Based on our inspection, it was concluded
that no immediate dam safety-related items need to be addressed. Be advised that we
may provide you with comments that develop as a result of our preparation of the dam
safety inspection report.
The 2025 Dam Safety Surveillance and Monitoring Report (DSSMR), prepared by
WSP, was submitted with AEP’s April 1, 2026 filing and reviewed after the inspection.
WSP has provided the following two recommendations to be included in the DSSMP.
• The DSSMR recommends that the DSSMP be updated to include a formal
bathymetry procedure.
• The DSSMR recommends that the DSSMP be updated to include a formal
procedure for documentation and remediation of animal burrows observed at
the site. As part of the formal procedure, an active log of all animal burrows
observed and remediated at the site should be kept. This active log should be
accompanied by an active plan set of all structures identifying the locations of
all animal burrows observed and repaired to date.

The DSSMR indicates that based on review of the 2025 data and observations,
there are no indications of the initiation or progression of an identified PFM, and the
water-retaining structures are performing satisfactorily. The DSSMR includes a statement
from the Chief Dam Safety Engineer that the dam is safe for continued operation. Our
review finds the 2025 DSSMR fulfills the requirements in Chapter 14 – Appendix K of
our engineering guidelines.
A revised DSSMP incorporating the recommendations mentioned above should be
submitted together with your 2026 DSSMR, which is due on April 1, 2027.
File your submittal using the Commission’s eFiling system at
https://www.ferc.gov/ferc-online/overview. When eFiling, select Hydro: Dam Safety and
Chicago Regional Office from the eFiling menu. The cover page of the filing must
indicate that the material was eFiled. For assistance with eFiling, contact FERC Online
Support at FERCOnlineSupport@ferc.gov, (866) 208-3676 (toll free), or (202) 502-8659
(TTY).
You may contact Mr. Eduardo Prieto at 312.596.4449 (Eduardo.Prieto@ferc.gov)
or me at (312) 596-4456 or if you have questions.
Sincerely,
Marilyn Sabido, P.E.
Regional Engineer
